source_review.notes: Checked the primary MapReduce, Google File System, and Mesos publications plus current Spark, Hadoop HDFS/YARN, and Kubernetes scheduling/storage documentation. All thirteen final cited URLs returned HTTP 200. Product locality levels and controls are attributed; general wait-versus-movement claims state assumptions.

evidence: Reviewed task j, object set O_j, node n, feasibility F, locality level ell, cost C, wait W, queue Q, transfer X, execution E, policy P, bytes B, throughput beta, latency L, request/decode terms, and wait bounds.
Checked GiB, GiB/s, seconds, bytes, percentages, costs, topology categories, and opportunity counts remain explicit.
Checked hard feasibility constraints are not numerically combined with soft preferences in ways that permit violation.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Cost components may require normalization to a common objective; the chapter explicitly permits reporting incomparable components separately.

evidence: Executed local-wait-versus-remote-transfer with Python 3.14.4 and reproduced 10-second transfer, choices wait-local/run-remote, and advantages 6/-10 seconds.
Recomputed Exercise 1 as 1.5+24/2 = 13.5 seconds and 5.5-second simple wait advantage.
Recomputed Exercise 3 cross-rack bytes as A=180 GiB, B=280 GiB, C=340 GiB.
Checked Jain/DRF or unrelated scheduling arithmetic is not reused as locality evidence.
numerical_recomputation.notes: Numerical comparisons intentionally exclude uncertain queues, heterogeneous execution, congestion externalities, caching, failures, fairness, and deadlines.

evidence: Verified the simple transfer expression L+B/beta plus request/decode terms has time/cost semantics under declared normalization.
Checked wait-local beats immediate remote only in the simplified model when expected wait is less than incremental remote cost.
Verified candidate feasibility must precede locality scoring, so timeout never relaxes hard residency/attachment/security rules.
Checked bounded time or qualifying-opportunity relaxation prevents indefinite soft-locality wait when scheduling continues.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: The simplified inequality is not presented as a production theorem; uncertainty and shared-resource effects require measurement.

evidence: Reviewed zero/huge inputs, one/many/no replicas, stale/corrupt locations, full local nodes, long/short tasks, and uncertain release.
Reviewed erasure reconstruction, shuffle fan-in, cache eviction, broadcast reuse, streaming state, volume attachment, and object-storage no-preference.
Reviewed hotspots, link/storage throttling, node/rack/zone failure, repair/recovery traffic, dynamic allocation, drain, and rescale.
Reviewed forged labels/locations, residency escape, unauthorized access, cross-tenant cache/shuffle, locality gaming, and metadata outage.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Performance preference, correctness ownership, residency/security, availability spread, fairness, and cost are reviewed independently.

evidence: Traced versioned object/partition locations through authoritative inventory, health/freshness, hard filtering, cost scoring, bounded delay, assignment, and invalidation.
Checked opportunities count only candidates feasible except for current soft-locality level and wait reset requires actual progress.
Checked replicas/fragments, cache, shuffle, state, and volumes preserve their distinct ownership and recovery semantics.
Checked actual allocation charges, temporal fairness deficit, dynamic executor lifecycle, and failure-domain policy remain enforced.
invariant_checking.notes: Selected locality is evidence only for a versioned path at decision time, not a timeless guarantee of access speed.

evidence: Reviewed the ten-step audit from byte inventory and topology through feasibility, cost, delay, data forms, scheduling interactions, security, and validation.
Checked simple wait-versus-transfer proof declares equal execution and no uncertainty/deadline assumptions.
Checked bounded relaxation liveness relies on qualifying opportunities and does not override hard policy.
Checked counterexamples for local slow devices, one local erasure fragment, aggregate shuffle, stale cache, and wrong-domain placement.
proof_review.notes: Primary system mechanisms are separated from the chapter's generic cost model and operational recommendations.

evidence: Audited local, process-local, node-local, rack-local, no-preference, remote, feasible, hard, soft, preferred, bounded, authoritative, and stale.
Confirmed topology categories are not mislabeled fixed performance metrics.
Confirmed object-store no-preference is not mislabeled zero movement/cost and one local erasure fragment is not labeled full locality.
Confirmed locality percentage is not mislabeled end-to-end performance, fairness, resilience, or cost proof.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: Claims name data/version, topology/path, access mode, decision time, and constraint/preference status where material.

evidence: Reviewed candidate rejection, locality rung/wait, predicted/actual movement, queue/start/execution, cache, retries, network/storage, fairness, and outcome metrics.
Confirmed no universal locality wait, bandwidth, topology cost, cache retention, replica preference, or scoring weight is prescribed.
Confirmed the executable fixture is not evidence for shared congestion, heterogeneous execution, placement feasibility, or production benefit.
Confirmed production acceptance requires topology-preserving traces, stale/failure/rescale/congestion injection, canaries, cross-tenant outcomes, and rollback.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: Locality is aggregated by bytes/time as well as task count and connected to job, cluster, reliability, security, and monetary outcomes.

conceptual_review.notes: Reviewed byte/state inventory, topology, hard/soft rules, feasibility, movement/wait estimates, delay scheduling, thresholds, replicas/erasure, cache/broadcast, shuffle/state/volumes, object stores, heterogeneity, fairness, elasticity, failures/hotspots, security, observability, and validation.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed implementable location metadata, candidate reason codes, progressive locality levels, cost calibration, block/state invalidation, executor decommission, topology-aware storage, congestion/hotspot telemetry, residency enforcement, trace replay, canary, and rollback. Internal practitioner-oriented review only.

pedagogical_review.notes: Verified progression from locality definitions and cost model through storage forms and scheduling interactions. Ten examples and five answered exercises cover wait/transfer, cache, replicas, erasure, shuffle, state, volumes, fairness, dynamic allocation, executable choice, and production review.

limitations: Internal evidence record only; no external MapReduce/GFS/Mesos/Spark/Hadoop/Kubernetes maintainer, scheduler/storage/network researcher, data-platform/SRE/FinOps/security/residency specialist, affected tenant, accessibility specialist, or certification review is claimed.
